transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because my family and my friends, they keep saying these bank papers prove nothing was taken. But I ain't stupid. For over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money. They’re using all these weird bills, and fundraisers, and trip plans to cover it up. 

Speaking of trips, my cousin keeps talking about going to the beach. I don't even know why anyone would want to go there, the sand gets absolutely everywhere. You bring one towel and next thing you know, your car floorboards are just covered in it. My mom used to have this old blue Chevy, and it took us weeks to vacuum it out after we went to the coast. The vacuum actually broke while we were doing it. The belt just snapped right in half, made this awful burning rubber smell. 

But anyway, I just have to keep confronting them. I'm gonna keep at it until they tell the truth about my money, because I see right through all those fake trip plans and bills.
Do you ever hear voices or see things that others don't hear or see?

No, I don't hear anything like that. No voices or seeing things. I just see what's right in front of me, you know? Like the receipts they leave lying around. Speaking of receipts, I went to the store the other day to get some milk, and the cashier gave me this receipt that was like three feet long. I mean, why do they print all those coupons on the back? Nobody uses them anyway. My neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, she clips coupons all the time, but she never remembers to bring them to the store. She’s got this little accordion folder full of them, organized by aisle. She showed it to me once when she was complaining about the price of cat food. She has three cats, and one of them is this mean old tabby that always tries to scratch my ankles when I walk by. I told her she needs to trim its claws, but she just says it's got a strong spirit. But yeah, no, no voices or anything. Just the truth about what they're doing with my money.

Do you ever find your thoughts jumping around so much that it's hard to follow them, or do people have trouble following what you're saying because your speech seems disorganized or hard to understand?

No, my thoughts don't jump around at all. I make perfect sense. If people don't understand me, it's just 'cause they ain't listening. Like that lady down at the post office. I went in there last week to get some stamps, the ones with the flowers on them, and she kept trying to give me the flag ones. I don't even like the flag ones. The sticky part on the back used to taste real bad when you had to lick 'em. Not that you gotta lick 'em anymore, they're mostly all peel-off stickers now. Which is good, honestly, 'cause my cousin swallowed a stamp once when we was kids. We was playing in my aunt's office and he just stuck it right on his tongue and accidentally swallowed it. He had to drink a whole giant glass of milk to wash it down, and he hates milk. Makes his stomach hurt real bad, he gets all cramped up for hours. But yeah, no, nobody has trouble following what I'm saying. I speak real clear, especially when I'm telling them I know what they're doing with my money.

Delusional disorder (F22.0) remains as the patient exhibits a fixed, false belief about money being hidden from them without other prominent psychotic features.

inference_history.note: The patient's statements suggest a preoccupation with a perceived conspiracy involving family and friends concealing the theft of their money, which points toward a delusional disorder (F22.0). The presence of bizarre or unusual content (e.g., interpreting everyday financial transactions as evidence of a cover-up) raises the possibility of schizophrenia (F20.0), especially if these beliefs are not well-organized. Brief psychotic disorder (F23.0) is possible if the duration of symptoms is under 1 month, though current information does not confirm this. Shared delusional disorder (F24.0) is also considered if there is evidence of another person adopting the delusional beliefs. No definitive exclusion yet.
